verdict.rationale: Muse's own docs confirm a persistent memory about the user: it is stored in the user's VM, can be inspected, edited and downloaded, and a Forget skill removes specific topics or people. The side-chats note implies context is shared across chats by default, but how remembered context is applied in new conversations is not documented. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of cross-chat recall in new conversations, controls over what gets remembered, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can have the assistant remember relevant context from previous chats and apply it in new conversations

citations.quote: You can inspect, edit and download these files freely, including Muse’s memory about you.
You can also use the Forget skill to have Muse forget information about specific topics or people.
some people still wanted separate context for certain topics — which made sense as projects grew more complex. So we built side chats.
